code.originalText: Review three weeks after surgical staging: final pathology and molecular class, genetic counseling, and the first cycle of dostarlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel

text.paragraph: Review three weeks after surgical staging, on the first treatment day. [S]

Ms. Ifill returns three weeks after robotic-assisted hysterectomy with removal of both tubes and ovaries, sentinel node mapping and removal of the enlarged para-aortic node. She went home the next morning, needed acetaminophen for about a week and nothing since, and has had no bleeding, fever, leg swelling or bladder trouble. She went back to work last week. The final pathology and molecular results are back, and the multidisciplinary tumor board reviewed them with Dr. Delacroix. She saw the genetic counselor this morning. She came today for her first cycle of dostarlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

Postmenopausal bleeding for three weeks, about eight years after her last period, in a woman of 60 who takes no hormone therapy: endometrial cancer must be excluded. Office endometrial biopsy taken today, transvaginal ultrasound this week, and gynecologic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom of her real illness was made public. Superseded by the diagnosis at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

S — Synthetic histology, molecular result and extent; her family gave endometrial cancer as the cause of death (D), and nothing more about it was made public.

list.item:
Endometrioid endometrial cancer, FIGO 2013 stage IIIC2ii, molecular class MMRd (C54.1). Surgery confirmed nodal spread to the pelvis and the para-aortic region, stage IIIC2ii; the molecular class does not change the stage at stage III but chooses the treatment. For mismatch repair deficient advanced disease, adding a PD-1 inhibitor to carboplatin and paclitaxel greatly lowers the risk of progression, so the tumor board recommends dostarlimab with chemotherapy for six cycles, then dostarlimab alone. Radiation is not planned now and will be reconsidered only if the end-of-treatment CT shows residual nodal disease. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests were negative. Counts, kidney and liver function, magnesium, TSH and free T4 allow full-dose treatment: creatinine 0.78 mg/dL, estimated creatinine clearance about 90 mL/min. [S]
Cycle 1 today: dostarlimab 500 mg, then carboplatin AUC 5 (575 mg) and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 (320 mg), every 21 days for six cycles.
Fosaprepitant, palonosetron and dexamethasone before each cycle; ondansetron at home as needed.
Temperature twice a day for a week after each cycle; call at once for 38.0 °C or more.
Report diarrhea, rash, cough, breathlessness or unusual tiredness at once: possible immune-related effects.

Pelvic and para-aortic nodal metastases (C77.8). Both enlarged nodes removed; no other node involved. Lymphedema risk is low after sentinel mapping but not zero after para-aortic node removal. [S]
Lymphedema check at each visit; report leg or genital swelling.

Follow-up: Cycles every 21 days in the infusion center, with blood counts, chemistry, TSH and a morning cortisol before cycle 2. Primary care and gynecologic oncology review at cycle 4. Call at once for a temperature of 38.0 °C or more, diarrhea, rash, cough or breathlessness. Next scheduled visit 2016-04-28: midpoint of combination treatment: blood counts, immune-related adverse event checks, neuropathy, and mood. [S]
